To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a new test for measuring the ability of patients to perform a functional task, the 6MWT, is feasible, reliable, valid, and responsive; (2) it correlates strongly with the distance walked on the 6-minute walk test, but it is a more demanding task and is therefore more likely to detect change; and (3) patients who have undergone a cardiac rehabilitation programme can perform this test safely, and it may be a useful outcome measure in future studies of cardiac rehabilitation

(1) physical performance tests (eg, single leg squat, hop tests) have not been validated to predict injury or rehabilitation outcomes; (2) psychometrics, a well developed framework for developing clinical assessment, could be applied to physical performance tests; and (3) the use of psychometrics may increase the validity and predictive value of physical performance tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to physical performance tests, and the development of a novel approach to the development of the physical performance test.
the development, evaluation and application of physical performance testing.
the relationship between psychological variables and physical performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) and the Functional Movement Screen (FMS) are valid and reliable tools for screening athletes and patients.
the Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) is a valid, reliable, and sensitive tool for identifying individuals who are at increased risk of ACL injury during sports activities.
there are currently no valid and reliable PPTs that are sensitive enough to detect changes over time or to predict future injuries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a long way to go before we can confidently use physical performance tests to predict injury risk or to guide treatment.
the Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) was a good predictor of ACL injury in female athletes, but not in males.

psychometrics may have a role in developing physical performance tests in sports medicine and that the field of sports medicine would benefit from the addition of a psychologist to the multidisciplinary sports medicine team.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of sports medicine should not be limited by the tools available to us We should be open to using the best tool for the job, whether it be an instrument or a test of physical performance.
we need more research on how to best assess physical performance in athletes.
we need a more comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms underlying the relationship between the physical and psychological domains.
